outcome.answer: The closest way to measure this is to test whether the model can reliably apply externally provided rules in new contexts, using benchmarks that compare performance on rule-based learning versus example-based learning [1, 2, 3, 4]. One paper introduces a benchmark for step-level procedural rule reasoning and evaluates single-rule, multi-rule, and multi-hop settings to measure how well models understand and use given rules [2]. Another shows that models can learn unseen rules in a controlled setting where interpolation fails, which helps separate genuine rule learning from pattern matching [3]. A broader probe suite also measures limits on what text-trained models can learn, including cases where rules are non-identifiable or unreachable by standard training [4].
